title: add-token-runway-predictor-and-alert-shelving
author: Priya Malhotra
release_notes: Adds tenant-level token runway prediction, a conservative alert-shelving controller to mute noisy cost alerts, and new dashboard panels to visualize runway and forecasted token usage.
description:
Motivation: On many short, high-variance workloads we observe noisy cost/alert churn tied to brief token bursts; teams want a way to surface forecasted token consumption so we can mute low-confidence alerts and reduce noise to oncall. This PR introduces a lightweight token runway predictor (streaming exponential smoothing ensemble), a conservative alert shelving controller, and a token-runway dashboard + runbook.

What changed (high level): added a streaming predictor sidecar that consumes token-usage metrics, exposes a per-tenant 'runway_hours' gauge and a 3-bin forecast histogram; added an alert-shelving component that can auto-shelve cost/SLO alerts for a short window when runway predictions and spike heuristics indicate transient noise; added dashboard panels to Console for runway, forecast distributions, and recent shelf events; extended metrics exporter to publish runway metrics; added unit, integration and e2e tests; added helm chart and deploy docs.

Why this approach: we intentionally kept the predictor deterministic and interpretable (no opaque ML model) to minimize operational risk and make audit/replay simple. Shelving is conservative by default (max 10 minutes, requires audit entry) to avoid hiding real regressions. Feature is gated behind per-cluster and per-tenant flags for staged rollout.

Testing and validation: unit tests for predictor math, integration tests for the streaming path, and an e2e that runs a synthetic token-burst workload to validate that shelving triggers and generates audit entries. Perf profiling shows the sidecar increases CPU by ~6-8% under worst-case ingestion (benchmarked on a small cluster); we added resource limits and a backpressure config.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy on staging with flag enabled for internal tenants. 2) Run the synthetic replay and validate dashboards/audit. 3) Gradual enablement for low-traffic tenants for two weeks with telemetry monitoring. 4) Enable broader rollout and monitor SLO regressions.

Notes: design doc and runbook linked in docs/observability/token-runway.md. This PR is focused on observability and SRE ergonomics; it does not change billing calculations or tenant quotas.

patch_summary: Introduce token runway forecasting pipeline, alert-shelving controller with conservative defaults, dashboard panels and runbook. Add unit, integration, and e2e tests. Helm chart updates to deploy predictor sidecar; metrics exporter changes to publish runway metrics.
design_notes: Predictor: exponential-smoothing ensemble with short/mid/long windows; exposes runway_hours gauge and a 3-bin forecast histogram (short/med/long). Shelving: triggered when runway_hours < configurable threshold AND a short-term spike detector indicates transient cost burst. Shelving writes audit events and sets a TTL (default 10m). Feature-flagged per-cluster and per-tenant.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect prediction could hide real regressions. Mitigation: conservative defaults (max 10m shelving), mandatory audit entries, optional manual un-shelve action in Console.
Risk: added CPU and memory pressure on telemetry nodes. Mitigation: run predictor as resource-limited sidecar with backpressure and circuit-breaker; feature-flag staging rollout and monitor metrics.
Risk: alert complexity increases for oncall. Mitigation: clear runbook, dashboard surfacing of recent shelf events, and a visible indicator on alerts that they were auto-shelved.
manual_steps: 1) Helm upgrade using scripts/deploy/predictor-helm.yaml to deploy sidecar. 2) Enable feature flag 'token_runway' via Console feature flags for target tenants. 3) Verify dashboards: Console -> Observability -> Token Runway. 4) Run synthetic e2e on staging and validate audit events. 5) Follow rollout plan in docs/observability/token-runway.md.
